To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of patient companions as interprets in ED consultations has the potential to cause misunderstandings and misdiagnoses.
patient companions are not always accurate interpreters.

(1) the use of patient companions for interpreting in emergency departments (ED) consultations is widespread; (2) the quality of interpreting varies greatly, with the most common errors being answering for the patient and omission of information; (3) the nature and severity of impact of the errors varies, with the omission of information having the greatest impact on clinical decisions; (4) the impact of errors on doctor patient relationships was also negative.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of patient companions in EDs and the impact that they have on the quality of care provided to linguistically diverse patients.
the quality of communication in the ED.
the role of the companion in the communication process and the potential risks associated with their involvement in medical consultations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of communication between the doctor and the patient was not satisfactory in the majority of cases.
the use of patient companions as interprets in the Emergency Department should be avoided.
the quality of communication in ED consultations that rely on patient companions is poor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the patient companions did provide useful information to the doctors, but the doctors were unaware of this information, and therefore did not take advantage of it.
patient companions are not always reliable interpreters and their use may have unintended negative consequences for the doctor patient relationship.
patient companions are not a substitute for professional interpreters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quality of communication in the ED is highly influenced by the nature and quality of the interpreting process.

the quality of interpreting services is a complex issue, involving the quality of the interpreting service itself, as well as the quality of the doctor patient relationship, and that these issues are interrelated.
EDs should be prepared for the possibility that patient companions may not be reliable interpreters.
